recall_prompt: Say how you would find n when n P 3 is 1320.
insider_note: The first mark is the factoring: 1320 as three consecutive factors, 12 · 11 · 10, with n the largest of them. A factoring such as 20 · 66 is correct arithmetic, but its factors are not consecutive, so no ⁿP₃ can be read from it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write 1320 as three consecutive factors
steps.margin_note: First mark. ⁿP₃ is a product of 3 consecutive whole numbers counting down from n. Break 1320 into such a product: 12 · 11 · 10.

recall.must_convey: That n P 3 is n times n minus 1 times n minus 2, and 1320 is 12 times 11 times 10.
accept: n P three is n into n minus one into n minus two and thirteen twenty is twelve times eleven times ten
write thirteen twenty as twelve into eleven into ten which is twelve P three
break one thousand three hundred twenty into three consecutive numbers twelve eleven ten
thirteen twenty ni twelve eleven ten ga rayali, adi twelve P three
three consecutive factors of thirteen twenty are twelve, eleven and ten

steps.why: ⁿP₃ has exactly three factors, each one less than the last, so matching 1320 to such a product identifies n at once without solving a cubic.
common_mistakes: Writing ⁿP₃ = n(n − 1)(n − 2)(n − 3) — that is ⁿP₄.
Factoring 1320 as 2 · 660 or 20 · 66, which are not consecutive.

steps.label: Compare and state n
steps.margin_note: Second mark. ⁿP₃ = ¹²P₃, so n = 12.

recall.must_convey: That comparing n P 3 with 12 P 3 gives n = 12.
accept: compare with twelve P three so n is twelve
the first factor is twelve so n is twelve
twelve P three tho compare cheste n twelve
n is the largest factor, twelve

steps.why: ⁿP₃ increases with n, so only one n can give 1320; the largest factor of the consecutive product is n.
common_mistakes: Answering n = 10, the smallest factor, instead of the largest.
Leaving the answer as ¹²P₃ without stating n.
